s03-2.old: Plan the repair step by step so nothing is missed, while others do the climbing
s03-2.new: Plan the repair step by step and list the parts needed, rewriting it as things change
s03-2.why: Cost was that others do the climbing, so the C card read as shirking (blind rating 2, lowest in scene). The new cost is real effort, and 'so nothing is missed' (a C cue) is removed.

s04-4.old: Test different apple blends and work out which one tastes best, and why
s04-4.new: Test apple blends to find which one tastes best
s04-4.why: At 73 characters it was about 25 longer than its scene-mates, so it stood out. 'and why' was an I cue.

s06-2.old: Examine the old machine to learn its use, even if the stall opens without you
s06-2.new: Examine the old machine to learn its use, though it may turn out to be junk
s06-2.why: 'even if the stall opens without you' framed the I card as neglecting duty. The new cost falls on the task, not on the others.

s08-2.old: Track the cloth rolls so none go missing before market day, a slow, careful job
s08-2.new: Track the cloth rolls for market day, recounting whenever the totals don't match
s08-2.why: 'a slow, careful job' calls the task itself dull, which lowers its desirability. 'so none go missing' repeats the C purpose-clause cue.

s09-1.old: Capture the cliff's changing light in drawings, even if it means climbing last
s09-1.new: Draw a picture map of the glowing cliff for the climbers, redrawing it as the light shifts
s09-1.why: The A card did nothing toward the scene goal and 'climbing last' read as selfish (rated 2, odd one out). Now the art serves the group, with a creative cost.

s09-2.old: Split the climbers into teams and set the pace, taking the blame if anyone is late
s09-2.new: Split the climbers into teams and set the pace, though some will grumble at your choices
s09-2.why: 'taking the blame' is the second E blame cost (also s02-4) and the heaviest-sounding in the scene (cost 4). Swapping it for a lighter cost also breaks the blame-means-E pattern.

s10-1.old: Weigh and record what salt is left, a fiddly job with the crowd shouting nearby
s10-1.new: Weigh what salt is left so each trader's loss is clear, with the crowd shouting nearby
s10-1.why: Recording during a dispute looked useless (rated 2). Tying the weighing to settling the loss makes the C card part of the solution.

s11-4.old: Lead the club night and persuade new people to join
s11-4.new: Run the club night and sign up new members
s11-4.why: 'persuade' is an E trigger already flagged in round 1 and still used twice (s04-2, s11-4).

s12-3.old: Teach children to care for the plants through stories
s12-3.new: Show children how to care for the plants through stories
s12-3.why: 'Teach children ... through games/stories' repeats s04-1 almost word for word, which is a cross-scene S cue.

s13-1.old: Proofread each page and keep the print run on time, with little praise if it goes well
s13-1.new: Proofread each page before printing, starting over whenever a mistake slips through
s13-1.why: 'with little praise' is a status cost that makes C look thankless. 'keep ... on time' repeats s15-4, another C cue.

s14-3.old: Sit up with the sick travellers and comfort them, missing a night's sleep
s14-3.new: Sit with the sick travellers and talk with them, though some would rather be left alone
s14-3.why: Dominant in a healing house: losing a night's sleep is a noble sacrifice that raises the card's appeal. A rejection cost keeps it S but makes it less of a moral must-pick.
